my_error_in_R129.what_I_said: the boolean Synergy flag and the delta EMAX quartile correlate at about 0.83, so counting criteria is redundancy
my_error_in_R129.what_R128_actually_measured: the FOUR continuous delta metrics (delta AUC, delta EMAX, delta fAUC, delta XMID) correlate at 0.806 to 0.967 among themselves; delta AUC versus delta EMAX is 0.831
my_error_in_R129.what_this_round_measures: the BOOLEAN FLAG versus the delta EMAX quartile correlates at only 0.199 overall and 0.292 in the smallest pool
my_error_in_R129.the_conflation: I carried the number 0.83 from a continuous-versus-continuous comparison into a boolean-versus-quartile claim without measuring it
my_error_in_R129.severity: the R129 reading rule is wrong and inverts the correct reading

the_correct_facts.fact_1_continuous_metrics_are_redundant: the four delta metrics measured 0.806 to 0.967 apart (R128) - they are four scalings of one readout

fact_2_the_two_criteria_are_largely_inde.reading: the boolean flag fires on 1.4 percent of keys while the quartile fires on 25 percent, and their overlap is only 5.6 to 12.2 percent, so they index different things

the_correct_facts.consequence: multi-criteria phrasing was substantially correct after all; the two criteria carry largely independent information, and R129 over-corrected in the opposite direction

what_survives_and_what_falls.falls: the CRITERION_REDUNDANCY rule added in R129, and the claim in C98 that the two criteria were never independent
what_survives_and_what_falls.survives: the C98 finding that the four continuous delta metrics are not independent endpoints (0.806 to 0.967), which is what the objective's 'independent functional endpoints' requirement turns on
what_survives_and_what_falls.unaffected: the frozen claim, which rests on the dense criterion plus random, permuted and dead-block controls
